question.problem:
The signed curvature of the plane curve $r(t)=⟨1-2t,\,{e}^{2t}⟩$ is given by

$$
k(t)=\frac{\bbox[2pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}}{\sqrt{(1+{e}^{4t})^{3}}}.
$$

What is the missing part of the expression?
question.worked_solution:
The signed curvature $k(t)$ of a plane curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t)⟩$ is given by

$$
k(t)=\frac{{x}^{′}(t){y}^{″}(t)-{y}^{′}(t){x}^{″}(t)}{([{x}^{′}(t)]^{2}+[{y}^{′}(t)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

Along our curve, we have

$$
x(t)=1-2t,\,y(t)={e}^{2t}.
$$

First, we calculate the derivatives of the components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =-2,\, & {y}^{′}(t) & =2{e}^{2t} \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =0,\, & {y}^{″}(t) & =4{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the signed curvature, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}k(t) & =\frac{-2\cdot 4{e}^{2t}-0\cdot 2{e}^{2t}}{{((-2)^{2}+(2{e}^{2t})^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{-8{e}^{2t}}{{(4+4{e}^{4t})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{-8{e}^{2t}}{8{(1+{e}^{4t})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{-{e}^{2t}}{\sqrt{(1+{e}^{4t})^{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$
